newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman says will increase use of DEIP.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman says will increase use of DEIP.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday that he will step up use of the Dairy Export Incentive Program this year.

In a press conference before addressing the annual convention of the American Farm Bureau Federation, Glickman said the department has already stepped up beef and dairy export program sales, as well as nonfat dry milk sales under the program.
Glickman said the agency will also use DEIP to stimulate sales of butter fat. The department has not granted any subsidies on butter fat sales since mid-1995.

"We will also work with private voluntary groups to increase the flow of dairy products into our international food assistance programs," Glickman said in the text of his speech to be delivered to the convention.
Glickman said in the press conference that the department will announce the new regulations of the Conservation Reserve Program by mid to late January.
"I think people will find these rules fair," he said. He said the goal of the CRP is to protect America's most fragile farmland.
"My guess is that you are going to see a (CRP) signup commence no later than about 60 days from now," he said. Glickman said it will be a five- to six-week signup period.
Glickman also said in the press conference that he doubts there will be any major changes in U.S. agricultural policy, which was revamped last year by the Freedom to Farm legislation.
"I do not look for any radical changes in the farm bill," he said.
"My feeling is the framework of Freedom to Farm will stand," Glickman said, but he noted there could be some minor legislative changes.
He said, however, that the department has not yet proposed any specific changes. "I have none right now ... I am not proposing anything."
Glickman indicated, as he has done before, that there could be some "safety net" changes, possibly with regards to crop insurance.
